**Hierarchy Construction:** Build a spatial hierarchy (such as an octree) over the scene geometry.
**Aggregation:** For each node, aggregate the properties of its child Gaussians.
**Traversal and Selection:** During rendering, traverse the hierarchy to select the appropriate level of detail (LoD) for each view.
**Splatting:** Render the selected Gaussians using standard 3DGS splatting techniques.
*   **Hierarchy Depth:** Determines the number of resolution levels.
*   **Aggregation Method:** How child Gaussians are merged into parent nodes.
*   **Limitations:** The specific implementation details (e.g., exact aggregation formulas, traversal algorithms) are not provided in the sources.
*   **When to use:** When rendering very large datasets in real time is required.
*   **When not to use:** When high-fidelity, non-hierarchical rendering is needed without memory constraints.
The concept of hierarchical 3D Gaussian representations is part of the broader effort to scale 3D Gaussian Splatting to city-scale scenes.
It builds on [CityGaussian / VastGaussian / DoGaussian](6143-citygaussian-vastgaussian-dogaussian.md), which divides the city into tiles and uses a LoD pyramid for streaming.
